abstract: Heterobifunctional proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) enable degradation of disease-relevant proteins but have largely been limited to cytosolic targets. Using reporter cell lines and the dTAG system to recruit cytosolic E3 ligases, we found that luminal substrates are resistant to degradation, whereas ER membrane proteins are efficiently degraded across multiple topologies. CRISPR screens confirmed dependence on cullin-RING ligases but did not identify canonical ER-associated degradation (ERAD) components, except the AAA ATPase VCP. Combined loss of DERL1/2/3 and depletion of HRD1 did not impair degradation, further supporting independence from canonical ERAD machinery. Mechanistic studies showed that ubiquitination is required for VCP binding and that removal of ubiquitin chains releases VCP, suggesting direct extraction of ubiquitinated substrates. An atorvastatin-cereblon PROTAC induced VCP-dependent degradation of HMGCR, preventing its compensatory accumulation during statin treatment. Together, these findings support a model in which ubiquitination by a cytosolic E3 ligase is sufficient to engage VCP and drive extraction, potentially bypassing canonical ERAD machinery.
